raw.details:
THE OUTPOST

One Problem. One Builder. Six Hours.

THE OUTPOST is a 6-hour, fully online, individual frontend development hackathon organized by Frontend Arena, designed to challenge participants to turn creative ideas into functional, visually impressive, and user-friendly web experiences.

Inspired by the spirit of exploration, strategy, and teamwork-free individual competition, THE OUTPOST gives every participant the opportunity to showcase their frontend development skills, creativity, and problem-solving abilities through a time-bound coding mission.

Participants will receive a problem statement at the beginning of the hackathon and must independently design, develop, test, and submit their solution within the allotted six hours.

This is an individual competition. Every participant builds their own project, submits their solution, and competes against other participants based on the quality of their implementation.

Hackathon Format

Duration: 6 Hours
Mode: Fully Online
Participation: Individual
Domain: Frontend Web Development
Challenge Format: Problem Statement-Based
Participation Fee: Completely Free
Evaluation: Defined Hackathon Evaluation Criteria
Competition: Individual Project Submission

Participants will receive the challenge at the beginning of the event and will have six hours to understand the requirements, plan their approach, build the application, test its functionality, and refine the final experience before submission.

The Frontend Mission

THE OUTPOST focuses on building modern, interactive, and visually polished web applications.

Participants must transform the given problem statement into a working frontend solution that demonstrates creativity, usability, functionality, and strong design decisions.

The goal is not simply to create a webpage. Participants should build an experience that solves the given problem while demonstrating their ability to make effective technical and design decisions under time constraints.

Modern Technology Requirement

THE OUTPOST is designed around modern frontend development practices.

Participants are required to use a modern frontend framework, library, or technology stack to build their projects.

Examples of acceptable technologies include:

  • React

  • Next.js

  • Vue

  • Nuxt

  • Svelte

  • SvelteKit

  • Angular

  • Astro

  • Remix

  • TypeScript

  • Tailwind CSS and modern styling frameworks

  • Modern UI and component libraries

  • Animation and interaction libraries such as Framer Motion

  • Other suitable modern frontend technologies

Participants may choose the technology stack that best suits their solution, provided it meets the hackathon requirements.

Standalone Technologies Are Not Permitted as the Primary Stack

The following are not permitted as the primary project stack:

  • Raw HTML-only projects

  • Raw CSS-only projects

  • Vanilla JavaScript-only projects

  • Static HTML/CSS/JavaScript websites without a modern framework or technology stack

HTML, CSS, and JavaScript may naturally be used within modern frameworks, but the project must be built using a suitable modern frontend stack.

Vibe Coding and AI-Assisted Development

Participants may use modern development tools to accelerate their workflow and improve productivity.

Permitted tools and resources include:

  • AI coding assistants

  • Vibe Coding platforms

  • Code editors and development environments

  • UI design and prototyping tools

  • Component libraries and design systems

  • Animation and interaction libraries

  • Public documentation and learning resources

  • Debugging and testing tools

  • Other relevant frontend development tools

Participants are responsible for understanding, testing, and validating the code they submit. The use of AI tools does not replace the need for a functional, well-designed, and technically sound solution.

Evaluation Criteria

Submissions will be evaluated using the following criteria:

1. UI/UX Design and Visual Quality
Visual consistency, layout, typography, spacing, usability, and overall presentation.

2. Functionality
Working interactions, navigation, core features, and implementation of the required functionality.

3. Creativity and Innovation
Original ideas, thoughtful design choices, and creative approaches to solving the problem.

4. Problem Statement Alignment
How effectively the project addresses the given challenge and fulfills its requirements.

5. Code Quality and Technical Implementation
Code structure, maintainability, appropriate use of technologies, and overall implementation quality.

6. Responsiveness and Accessibility
Usability across different screen sizes, responsive layouts, and attention to accessibility.

The final evaluation will follow the official criteria and scoring framework announced by the organizers.

How THE OUTPOST Works

01 — The Brief
Receive the official problem statement at the beginning of the hackathon.

02 — Plan
Understand the requirements and decide how to approach the challenge.

03 — Build
Develop your solution using an eligible modern frontend technology stack.

04 — Test and Improve
Validate functionality, refine the UI, fix issues, and improve the overall user experience.

05 — Submit
Submit your completed project through the official submission process before the deadline.

06 — Evaluation
The submitted projects are assessed according to the official hackathon evaluation criteria.

07 — Results
Final results are determined according to the organizers' announced evaluation and ranking process.

Rules and Guidelines

  • THE OUTPOST is an individual participation hackathon. Team submissions are not permitted.

  • The total development period is six hours.

  • The event is conducted fully online.

  • Participation is completely free.

  • Participants must build a solution relevant to the provided problem statement.

  • A modern frontend framework, library, or technology stack is mandatory.

  • Raw HTML-only, CSS-only, and Vanilla JavaScript-only projects are not permitted as the primary stack.

  • AI-assisted development and Vibe Coding tools are permitted.

  • Participants may use suitable public libraries, frameworks, documentation, and development resources.

  • Participants must ensure that their projects are functional and ready for evaluation.

  • Projects should be developed within the official hackathon duration.

  • Participants must not submit plagiarized or substantially copied projects.

  • Any attempt to manipulate the evaluation process or compromise the integrity of the competition may result in disqualification.

  • Participants are responsible for testing their project and checking the submission requirements before submitting.

  • Submissions received after the official deadline may not be considered.

  • Participants must follow all instructions communicated by the organizers.

  • The final results will be determined according to the official evaluation process.

Who Can Participate?

THE OUTPOST welcomes individuals interested in:

  • Frontend Development

  • Web Development

  • UI/UX Design

  • Creative Coding

  • Modern JavaScript Frameworks

  • Vibe Coding

  • AI-Assisted Development

  • Rapid Prototyping

  • Building Digital Products

Whether you are a student, aspiring developer, experienced coder, or technology enthusiast, this is an opportunity to challenge yourself and demonstrate your ability to build under pressure.

The Challenge

At the beginning of the event, participants will receive a specific problem statement.

Your mission is to transform that brief into a creative, functional, responsive, and visually polished frontend experience within six hours.

Your project should demonstrate:

  • A clear understanding of the problem

  • Thoughtful design and user experience

  • Functional and meaningful interactions

  • Effective use of modern frontend technologies

  • Creativity and attention to detail

  • A reliable and well-tested implementation

The Final Mission

Six hours. One problem statement. One individual builder.

THE OUTPOST is your opportunity to think creatively, build strategically, and turn your ideas into a working digital experience.

Design. Develop. Deploy your creativity.

Welcome to THE OUTPOST — Your Mission Starts Here.

Organized by Frontend Arena.

prizes.others: Awarded to the Rank 1 participant on the final PROMPT RUN leaderboard in recognition of outstanding performance, creativity, and successful completion of the hackathon challenge.
Awarded to the Rank 2 participant for achieving one of the highest final scores and demonstrating strong technical execution and problem-solving.
Awarded to the Rank 3 participant for achieving a top position on the final leaderboard and delivering an impressive project.
Awarded to all participants who successfully participate in PROMPT RUN, recognizing their effort, creativity, and contribution to the hackathon.
